steps.text: 4:23 P.M. \ Cloudy, turning overcast
MacMartin Brothers' Chip, first floor

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Still no reply?

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: None. Haven't gotten a peep from Londinium, yesterday or today.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It's been twenty hours. They have to have received my last telecoms by now.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Could the encrypted line be faulty?

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Hard to say, sir. Being honest, it's been nearly ten years since I graduated, transferred to Hillock. There's not much information you need to activate this secret comms line.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Two years back, around the end, I reported to our group's boss, and he asked me if I had anything to say other than whatever number kid was being born. And that if I hadn't, I could save even giving the routine reports.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, no wonder you opened this chippy.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Not a bad plan, right? Codename's not Chef for fun. Thought at the time, suppose some outsider wanted to sniff out our liaison point, they'd only suspect next door's bookshop.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Aye, right. Besides, your chips are delicious too!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Ought to be, eh? Hahah, you fill yourselves up.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Hillock's potatoes are high quality. Locals all love my chips—if I didn't still remember my actual job as a lamplighter, I would've opened up branches ages ago. Five, six of them.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Ah, anyhow, I thought I was dreaming of the time I was in training again, when you gave the secret knock at the door yesterday.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...It seems highly likely this line was abandoned long ago.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Or perhaps, someone's received our info, but doesn't want to reply.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You mean there's people interceptin' our intel on purpose, Leader?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Not easy to say yet.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We'll send the next report as we would originally—right, and besides Triangle's findings, add on the outcome of my dialogue with Colonel Hamilton.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The Colonel's targeted measures against a portion of the residents are already extremely suspicious. In the worst case, I'd like for our team to be allowed more flexibility.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: That... sounds like there's no point in me convincing you to use a barracks Messenger, is there?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ugh. Leader, I don't wanna say this, but we're a little low on numbers.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: That definitely isn't like you to say. Relax, though. Nobody wants to take that step.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But... the circumstances about this city are far more complicated than any of us foresaw.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Chef, seeing as you've been in County Hillock for so long, how do you feel about the people here?

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Nothing unusual to me. If you put a Taran in front of me right now, I wouldn't fancy them much different from a Victorian anywhere else.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: To tell the honest truth, if life's not bad, who'd want to make trouble all the livelong day?

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Quite a few wear ideals on their sleeves, but only a minority ever take them to heart. Most just care about filling their stomachs, and if they're full, they can care about the purse, too.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Right you are! I can barely imagine Damian Barry caught up in the spectre force either.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: In my eyes, him and the locals were all normal people, scared stiff beggin' for forgiveness the moment they're arrested, comin' together when a loved one dies just so they could fall to pieces and weep.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: They're nothin' like trained soldiers at all.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What you're saying is exactly what I'm worrying about—Colonel Hamilton might have been spouting more than just alarmist talk.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: When ordinary people take up weapons, voluntarily or not, the disaster we then face will be the likes of which Victoria hasn't seen for a very long time.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Afternoon, Saoirse! Lucky me, I was just about to go find you at the newspaper.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Eh? What's wrong, Saoirse? Were you just crying?

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: Janie... No, I'm alright. I'm perfectly fine.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Pull the other one. Your eyes are all puffy, and your face is pale as sheets. The Saoirse I know would never be caught in the street looking this ghastly. Something gave you a nasty shock, didn't it?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Who bullied you? Was it that soldier from last time? I'll help you think of something... There has to be something.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: No, Janie, don't you fuss. He hasn't come bothering me again.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: It's... I don't know how to put it.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Come on, deep breaths—it's me right here, your very good friend. You're safe now, I promise.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: Janie... why? Why are you one of them?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: What are you talking about, Saoirse? I don't understand.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: I don't want you to get hurt. You're the best friend I have... and you're a good person. I'm good too, right? My ma, da, cousin... aren't we all good people?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Your cousin... Barry? You mean Damian Barry? I'm so sorry. I wasn't fast enough.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: It's not your fault. And I don't think it's mine. I just want to live life peaceful. I don't want to see any more people I care about die.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Cry it out, Saoirse... I'm here with you. Seeing a loved one pass on and still having to manage your work, it's too much pressure on you. Here, lean on my shoulder? It'll be more comfortable.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: That's okay, thank you, Janie, I'm much better just seeing you. I understand what I have to do now—

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: This is for you.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Is... this an address?

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: I could give you a few names, too. But there's no need. I don't want to put you in even more danger.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: This address should be enough. You can... hand it to someone you think's reliable. Your Sergeant Major, or maybe another officer, like Uncle Louis.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: I know there's people around asking about Damian. They want to be clear what it is we're plotting.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Plotting—Saoirse, even you...?!

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: I'm not sure. You can believe me or not—I've only been responsible for passing on some info some ways. A few notes stuck between book pages, one or two hidden signals in the Hillock Evening News's classifieds.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: I used to think this was for making everyone safer... I didn't twig what dreadful things they're scheming, not until the... dispatch I just heard by the chief editor...

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: Never mind that. I'm not trying to justify myself or even repent, what's important is that you stop them as soon as you can.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Alright, I will. I'm sure of who I should give this to. She'll fairly treat you all, more than anyone else would. Saoirse, don't be scared. Everything will be alright.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: Alright, Janie. I trust you.

steps.name: Saoirse
steps.text: Remember, it's 8 P.M. Hold onto this address tight—

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: East side of the statue at District Ten... third alleyway on the left. There's a bookshop there, with a flower pot by the door... yellow rose... found it.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: To... Bag... pipe—

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (Do I just leave it under the flowerpot like this and call it done? A loose brick right there, exactly like they said this morning.)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (This really is an unusual way of receiving your letters.)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (Friend from Londinium, I hope you can be of help to Saoirse... and all of us.)

steps.name: MacMartin Brothers Worker
steps.text: Boss, someone left a new slip downstairs, under the yellow rose.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Bring it in.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh, yellow rose? So it's for me? That was fast.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The informer you mentioned before?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Aye. She's a soldier at the barracks too, but I can assure you, Leader, she's warmhearted. She's good.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I... hope you've gotten an eye for people.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No worries! My eyesight's always been brilliant.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What's it say on the slip?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: '109 Dam St, tonight 8pm'—that's all.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Dam Street? It's the boundary between Districts Ten and Eleven. Rings bells for me—it's Baron Bolton's estate.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Looks like there's an important meeting tonight. Bagpipe, we should go.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: This is where you were...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That's right. Sipping hot tea, skimming the paper, doing things befitting a woman of my age.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Phew, strong wind kicking up.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Found what you were looking for?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: (Taran) When you want to find tomorrow, you go meet with yesterday.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: You can speak Taran?!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Can't speak much at all. What you hear is what you get. Just showing off what I learned.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Hard to believe... Oliver was right, you're an incredible one.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Hahah. You get a nice rush the first time you impress somebody, but there's diminishing returns on the second and third round.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Nobody at our office even knows how to speak Taran.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Considering your backgrounds, that's reasonable.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Oliver grew up in a middle-class household in north Londinium, with family roots in Gaul. He lives upstairs from the office these days, taking some time off every year to go back and see his wife and children.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Fred's more or less an apprentice from County Peninsula. He's got bunch of brothers and one little sister, and the whole family gets along like a dream.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Will's a local. His clan moved decades ago from a fixed village nearby, and his Taran blood's probably from his paternal grandmother.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: You've looked at our data?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Do I look like the type who does homework? Not my style.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Then... how do you know?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Language.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Name, pronunciation, wording, tone, and even where you pause—language tells a keen ear more than you could ever guess.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: I heard about how Sankta extraordinary are, but I never figured...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Ahah. Really, it's just a hobby of mine.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Anyhow, language itself holds a special significance to some folks. Why else would the Tarans have cared so much about digging a sample of their own language out of a pile of old books?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: You're not wrong. Half a decade ago, barely any Tarans regularly spoke it.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: And you?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: You've probably heard it in me... I'm not a Taran. My wife was. She only taught me a word or two while she was still alive.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Yet nowadays, you see that gradually dying language all over the newspaper.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Plus, I just overheard someone outside the window teaching kids how to call each other in Taran.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Until you mentioned it... I never noticed.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Language binds a people together tighter than most things. A language doesn't get diluted over time like bloodlines do, and it doesn't get weighed on the scales of cost-benefit analysis like everything else.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Looks like there's some out there who want to exploit those ties, bring back together the community that's been loosening away. But with that, the gatherings that already were, lose their stability.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Victoria won't just sit back and let this play out right under its nose. And yet, the harder you pull, the harder the backlash will snap.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You all know why I came, don't you?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Actually... I'm not that sure. I just feel like, you wouldn't need to bother an elite operator to go fetch data in person.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Numbers on paper don't mean a thing against seeing it with your own two eyes. Put it that way, I really am here fetching data.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Could you just tell me one more time, in the last six months, how many local businesses suspended collaboration with us?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Seven.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That's three on top of last month's report. In modern Victoria, when any wind stirs the grass, it's the big merchants' wallets that feel it first.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I need to head out, get a few more eyefuls of this place—make it before this city gets drowned under dirty rain.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Leader, you've had your eyebrows wrinkled ever since morning.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We don't have much time to go.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: This spectre force move is inconsistent in ways with past incidents.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Their execution was covert before, rapid. Every time we thought to chase them, we'd find the leads wiped clean.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But now...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, like they finished knittin' a jumper and just tossed yarn ends on the floor? Barely an idea of how each end is linked, too.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And moreover... these leads have all cut off at County Hillock.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: It's not just you. I'm feelin' trapped as all heck too.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: This city is just like a pressure cooker sealed shut. The residents, the barracks, everyone's twitchy, and people are gettin' up in arms anywhere and anytime.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Everyone's waiting. Waiting for when the first bolt strikes.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But if it does truly strike, what will this city... no, what will Victoria become?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (Leader...!)

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: (Hm?)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (Someone's tailin' us!)

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: (So they are... See that alley to the west?)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (Understood.)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Stop where you are!

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Urghh—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh, hold on, what? It's a little bairn... and you look kind of familiar, too?

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Uwgh, ow...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ah, sorry! I'll let go now. I thought it'd be some baddie followin' us.

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: ...Ball.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You dropped your ball, so you came here to pick it up?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'll ask you to hurry home now, it's not too safe here. Your mam and dad'll worry for you if you go runnin' all over.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: False alarm, Leader.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Just one child? No, that doesn't seem quite right.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It wasn't just one person following us, and the fact they could go several streets without us noticing means they definitely have experience tailing.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Did you see anyone out of the ordinary just now, when you hid up high?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ah... if I have to say, there was a street not far away with a particularly bright ring I caught a glimpse of...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...Sankta.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Lemme get a... piece of cake, and this apple pie... and I'll have some of those cookies, too.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Tough call... Warfarin has been telling me to lay off the sweets...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Hey there. Quick question, which of these cakes is the sweetest?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Like you don't know? C'mon, you've been in County Hillock a while, haven't you? If I had to guess, probably over three years of service—

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: Who are you?!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Calm down. I could tell, and the nice folks you're following sure could too.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Your cover's blown anyway. Why don't you try some of this apple pie I bought? It's good, I'm telling you.

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: You weird, mad Sankta. Where did you come from? Why are you trying to get in my way?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Me? I'm not, I'm just passing by.

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: Team 12, target lost, but judging by the direction they disappeared, it's likely they're heading for Dam Street.

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: Alright... I understand, I'll bring them straight away...

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: We'll check through one by one.

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: I'm warning you, Sankta, if it's not yours to meddle, don't meddle.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Warning me...?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: If I had a nickel for every time I heard that... You know, I ain't exactly used to walking around unarmed.

steps.name: Restless Youth
steps.text: ...I've got no time to listen to you talk big. Soldiers, we're moving.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You can breathe now, shopkeep. The soldiers are all gone.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Mind bagging up the sweets for me? I got some folks back at the office who oughta try them.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: After all... it's about time I called all my little friends back from their field work.
